pricing.faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
pricing.faq.card.q: Do I need a credit card to start?
pricing.faq.card.a: No. The Community plan is free forever and requires no payment details. The Pro trial also starts without a card.
pricing.faq.eventPass.q: What exactly does an Event Pass cover?
pricing.faq.eventPass.a: One competition, for as long as it’s running. The pass ({pass}) gives that competition 10 divisions and 128 entrants per division. You also get advanced formats, exports and realtime, a one-time AI credit top-up (+25 AI credits), and a 4% platform fee on its entry fees instead of Community’s 5% — and it stops counting against your free active-competition slot. A competition holds one pass and keeps it. Your club logo and card entry fees work on every plan already, pass or no pass. Other competitions in your org stay on Community limits.
pricing.faq.upgraded.q: I bought an Event Pass and later went Pro — what happens?
pricing.faq.upgraded.a: While you're on Pro, Pro's limits apply across the whole organisation — and on the competition you passed, the two are read together: whichever limit is higher wins, so nothing the pass bought is taken back. If you ever cancel Pro the pass carries that competition on its own, for as long as it is still running — a pass is tied to the competition it was bought for and stops with it.
pricing.faq.trialEnd.q: What happens when my Pro trial or subscription ends?
pricing.faq.trialEnd.a: Your org drops back to Community limits automatically. Nothing is deleted — competitions over the limit become read-only until you archive down to quota or upgrade again.
pricing.faq.fees.a: Yes, on every plan — Community included. What your plan buys is a cheaper cut: the platform fee is 5% on Community, 4% on a competition with an Event Pass, 2% on Pro. Connect your club's Stripe account and fees from online registration are paid out directly to the club.
pricing.faq.platformFee.q: What's the platform fee, and is it on top of Stripe's own fees?
pricing.faq.platformFee.a: It's {communityFee}% on Community, {passFee}% with an Event Pass, {proFee}% on Pro — charged on your paid entry fees. It's additive, not instead of Stripe: your club's connected Stripe account still pays Stripe's own processing fees on every charge, on top of our cut. Connect your club's Stripe account and payouts go straight to the club.
pricing.faq.groups.q: Can one subscription cover more than one organisation?
pricing.faq.groups.a: Yes. A subscription is a billing group: it can hold several organisations under one card and one invoice, and each organisation after the first costs no more than half your plan’s rate. Every organisation in the group runs on the group’s plan, so joining a Pro group takes an organisation’s entry-fee rate from 5% to 2%. Payouts are untouched — each organisation keeps its own Stripe account and its own bank details.
pricing.faq.currencies.q: Which currencies can I pay in?
pricing.faq.currencies.a: USD, EUR, GBP and INR — use the switcher above. Your first checkout pins the currency for future renewals.
pricing.faq.annual.a: Yes — a year up front costs less than ten monthly payments in every currency we bill in, so annual is more than two months free. It's the default on the Pro card above.
pricing.faq.cancel.a: Yes. Cancel from Settings → Billing. Your Pro access continues until the end of the billing period.

product.streaming.cam.1.p: The match is already named. A three second hold starts the broadcast, so a pocket cannot. Camera picture illustrated.
product.streaming.cam.2.p: Turn it on for a match and the phone goes live when play starts and stops at the result. Health of the link is on the same screen.
product.streaming.ticket.title: One match. One credit. About a coffee.
product.streaming.ticket.body: No monthly streaming fee. Buy a credit when you want a match on air, or a pack for the season. Streaming is on every plan, the free one included.
product.streaming.ticket.heading: Admit one match
product.streaming.ticket.stubBottom: Bigger packs cost less per match.
product.streaming.club.text: Seazn Demo Club runs a cricket league, a football league and a tennis open. Every score on it came through the real scoring pad.
product.streaming.club.alt: A competition's public page on Seazn Demo Club
product.streaming.faq.1.q: Do I need a camera crew?
product.streaming.faq.1.a: No. A phone on a tripod is enough. If you already use OBS, the score goes in as one browser source.
product.streaming.faq.2.q: Whose channel does it go out on?
product.streaming.faq.2.a: Yours. Viewers and subscribers stay with your club.
product.streaming.faq.3.a: One credit, which covers one match for up to 5 hours. Credits you buy never expire.
product.streaming.faq.4.a: Viewers see "Camera reconnecting, back shortly" and the broadcast carries on when the signal returns.
product.streaming.closing: Put your next match on air.
sport.cricket.meta.title: Cricket tournament software
sport.cricket.meta.description: Cricket tournament software: fixtures, ball-by-ball scoring from a phone, net run rate tables, DLS targets and a live page for everyone at the boundary. Free for small clubs.
sport.cricket.lede: Cricket tournament software: fixtures, ball-by-ball scoring, net run rate tables and a live page for everyone at the boundary. From a weekend cup to a league season.
sport.cricket.demo.title: One tap. Four screens.
sport.cricket.road.title: Built for how cricket is actually run
sport.cricket.road.lede: What the organiser, the scorer and the crowd each get.
sport.cricket.road.1.p: T20 or other limited-overs formats, overs a side, bowler limits, super over rules. Groups, Super 8, knockout: Seazn draws the fixtures.
sport.cricket.road.2.p: Runs, extras, wickets, reviews and retirements. The pad keeps striker, bowler and over, and takes back a mistake.
sport.cricket.road.3.p: At the crease, this over, partnership, the chase, full scorecard and commentary. No app and no login.
sport.cricket.road.3.cap: The public match page on a phone.
sport.cricket.phones.title: What the scorer holds
sport.cricket.phones.lede: The Seazn app on a phone at the boundary. Every picture here is the real app, scoring a real match.
sport.cricket.phones.1.p: Runs, the over so far and both batters, always in view.
sport.cricket.phones.2.p: How out, then who comes in next.
sport.cricket.phones.3.p: Wide, no-ball, bye and leg-bye, with runs run.
sport.cricket.phones.4.p: Reviews, powerplays, rain and revised targets.
sport.cricket.offline.title: No signal at the ground? Keep scoring.
sport.cricket.offline.lede: {app} holds every ball on the phone and sends them, in order, when the signal returns. Nothing is typed twice and nothing is lost.
sport.cricket.offline.1.p: The pad keeps working. A badge counts the balls waiting.
sport.cricket.offline.2.p: History marks each waiting ball as sending.
sport.cricket.offline.3.p: The balls go up by themselves. Everyone's screen catches up.
sport.cricket.offline.fig1: Airplane mode on. Five balls waiting.
sport.cricket.ticket.title: Net run rate, worked out for you.
sport.cricket.ticket.body: Standings sort by points, then wins, then net run rate, from the scores as they are entered. Rain cuts a match short? DLS targets are supported.
sport.cricket.ticket.heading: Cricket, properly
sport.cricket.ticket.stubBottom: Your YouTube channel, score on screen, about a coffee a match.
sport.cricket.club.text: Open the Southend Premier League on Seazn Demo Club: scorecards, commentary and tables, all from real scoring.
sport.cricket.club.alt: A cricket match page on Seazn Demo Club
sport.cricket.faq.1.q: Can I score ball by ball?
sport.cricket.faq.1.a: Yes. Runs, extras, wickets, reviews and retirements, with the striker and bowler tracked for you.
sport.cricket.faq.2.q: Do you work out net run rate?
sport.cricket.faq.2.a: Yes. Standings use points, then wins, then net run rate, computed from the scores.
sport.cricket.faq.3.a: DLS targets are supported for shortened matches.
sport.cricket.faq.4.a: T20 and other limited-overs formats, as a league, groups then knockout, or straight knockout.
sport.cricket.faq.5.a: Free forever for small clubs. Entry fees by card work on every plan.
sport.cricket.closing: Your first fixture list in minutes.
product.signal.label.phone: Score, then switch the signal off
product.remote.meta.title: Score from a phone, even with no signal
product.remote.meta.description: Hand any match to a volunteer's phone with a QR code. No account. The Seazn app keeps scoring with no signal and sends every tap when it returns.
product.remote.lede: Score from a phone, even offline. Hand a match to anyone with a QR code, no account needed. In {app} the pad keeps working with no signal and sends every tap, in order, when it returns.
product.remote.demo.title: Switch the signal off. Keep tapping.
product.remote.demo.note: A working model of the real app. Nothing here is recorded.
product.remote.road.title: From your screen to their phone
product.remote.road.lede: Three steps, each shown on the real screen.
product.remote.road.1.p: Open the match and choose Remote scoring. Show the QR, print it on the scoresheet, or send the link.
product.remote.road.2.p: No account and nothing to set up. The code scores this one match, until it is final.
product.remote.road.3.p: Every tap reaches the public match page. Only you can make the result final, and you can cancel a code at any time.
product.remote.road.3.cap: The public match page on a phone.
product.remote.offline.title: What it looks like on the day
product.remote.offline.lede: These are the real app with airplane mode on, mid-match. Five balls scored with no connection, then sent when it came back.
product.remote.ticket.title: Free. On every plan.
product.remote.ticket.body: Scoring never costs anything, from a desk or from a volunteer's phone. One code per match.
product.remote.ticket.heading: One code, one match
product.remote.faq.1.q: Does the volunteer need an account?
product.remote.faq.1.a: No. They scan the code or open the link, and score.
product.remote.faq.2.a: No. The link opens a scoring pad in the phone's browser. Scoring with no signal needs the Seazn app.
product.remote.faq.3.q: What happens when the phone loses signal?
product.remote.faq.3.a: In the Seazn app the pad keeps working. Taps wait on the phone and send themselves, in order, when signal returns.
product.remote.faq.4.q: Can a volunteer change the result?
product.remote.faq.4.a: They score the match. Only you can make it final, and the code stops working once you do.
product.remote.offline.1.p: The pad keeps working. A badge counts the balls waiting.
product.remote.offline.2.p: History marks each waiting ball as sending.
product.remote.offline.3.p: The balls go up by themselves. Everyone's screen catches up.
product.remote.offline.fig1: Airplane mode on. Five balls waiting.
product.remote.ticket.stubBottom: Your YouTube channel, score on screen, about a coffee a match.
product.format.meta.title: Tournament formats: league, knockout, groups and Swiss
product.format.meta.description: Say how many teams, pitches and hours you have. Seazn shows which tournament formats fit your day and draws every match for you.
product.format.lede: Eight teams, two pitches, one morning: league, knockout, or groups and a final? Put in your numbers. Seazn shows which formats fit the time you have, then makes the whole draw for you.
product.format.demo.title: Say what you have. See what fits.
product.format.demo.note: The same sums Seazn does when you set up a competition.
product.format.road.title: From a guess to a full draw
product.format.road.lede: Three steps, each shown on the real screen.
product.format.road.1.p: Enter teams, pitches and hours. Each format shows its matches and how long it takes, before you commit to anything.
product.format.road.1.cap: Choosing a format for a new division.
product.format.road.2.h: The draw is made for you
product.format.road.2.p: Rounds, groups and brackets are generated in one go. Winners move on by themselves as results come in.
product.format.road.2.cap: A knockout draw on its public page.
product.format.road.3.p: One link shows the schedule, the tables and who plays next. No app and no login.
product.format.ticket.title: The usual formats are free.
product.format.ticket.body: League, groups then knockout, knockout and Swiss are on every plan. Mix stages too: a league into a final, or a qualifier into a main draw.
product.format.ticket.heading: On every plan
product.format.ticket.stubBottom: And the rarer ones: page playoff, Americano and ladders.
product.format.faq.1.a: Enter your teams, pitches and hours. Seazn marks the format that fits and gives everyone the most play.
product.format.faq.2.q: What if the number of teams is odd?
product.format.faq.2.a: It still works. Leagues give a team a rest each round, and brackets give byes to the top seeds.
product.format.faq.3.a: Yes. Groups can feed a knockout, a league can end in a final, and a knockout can have a plate for first-round losers.
product.format.faq.4.q: Who works out the tables and who goes through?
product.format.faq.4.a: Seazn does, from the scores. Tie-breaks follow the sport's own rules.
